title: CRISPR screen reveals FTO-mediated m6A modification of ATF3 as protective in ischaemic stroke
title_zh: CRISPR筛选揭示FTO介导的ATF3 m6A修饰在缺血性脑卒中中的保护作用
abstract: Abstract RNA modifications, especially N6-methyladenosine (m6A), have emerged as pivotal regulators of gene expression in neurological disorders, yet their roles in ischaemic stroke remain unclear. Here, we performed a CRISPR-Cas9 loss-of-function screen targeting 118 RNA modification-related genes in neuronal cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) and validated the findings in a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). We identified Fto as a top negatively selected gene, with its expression progressively reduced and global m6A levels increased during ischaemic injury. Neuron-specific Fto knockout aggravated infarct size, neurological deficits, cognitive impairment, and neuronal apoptosis, accompanied by activation of multiple signalling pathways revealed by RNA-seq analysis. Integrated m6A-seq and RNA-seq profiling uncovered Atf3 as a hypermethylated and upregulated hub gene downstream of Fto deficiency, linking m6A dysregulation to enhanced neuronal apoptosis. In vitro assays confirmed that FTO knockdown increased ATF3 mRNA methylation and expression under OGD/R conditions, whereas Fto overexpression in vivo alleviated ischaemic brain injury, improved neurological outcomes, reduced Atf3 expression, and lowered global m6A levels. Together, our findings reveal the Fto/m6A/ATF3 axis as a critical mediator of ischaemic injury and highlight Fto restoration as a potential therapeutic strategy for stroke.
abstract_zh: 摘要 RNA修饰，尤其是N6-甲基腺嘌呤（m6A），已成为神经疾病基因表达的关键调控因子，但其在缺血性脑卒中中的作用尚不清楚。我们在受氧-葡萄糖剥夺/再氧化（OGD/R）处理的神经细胞中，对118个与RNA修饰相关的基因进行CRISPR‑Cas9失活筛选，并在中大脑动脉闭塞/再灌注（MCAO/R）小鼠模型中验证了结果。筛选发现Fto是最显著的负向筛选基因，其表达随缺血损伤逐步下降，全球m6A水平升高。神经元特异性Fto敲除加剧了梗死面积、神经功能缺陷、认知障碍和神经元凋亡，并伴随多条信号通路的激活（通过RNA‑seq分析揭示）。整合m6A‑seq与RNA‑seq数据发现Atf3是Fto缺失下的高甲基化且上调的关键基因，将m6A失调与增强的神经元凋亡联系起来。体外实验证实，FTO敲低在OGD/R条件下增加ATF3 mRNA的甲基化和表达，而体内Fto过表达则减轻缺血性脑损伤、改善神经功能、降低Atf3表达并降低全球m6A水平。综上所述，我们的研究揭示了Fto/m6A/ATF3轴是缺血性损伤的关键介导因子，并提示恢复Fto功能可能成为脑卒中的潜在治疗策略。
